User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the SmartVest platform.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth of the user.

walletId.description: Reference to the user's Wallet. (Relationship: User 1:1 Wallet)

referrerId.description: Reference to the user who referred this user. (Relationship: User 1:N User (self-referential))

isAdmin.description: Indicates whether the user is an admin.

Package.title: Package
Package.description: Represents an investment package offered on the SmartVest platform.

weeklyProfitPercentage.description: Weekly profit percentage offered by the package.

referralBonusPercentage.description: Referral bonus percentage associated with the package.

UserPackage.title: UserPackage
UserPackage.description: Represents the association between a user and a purchased package.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user package.

userId.description: Reference to the User. (Relationship: User 1:N UserPackage)

packageId.description: Reference to the Package. (Relationship: Package 1:N UserPackage)

isActive.description: Indicates whether the package is currently active for the user.

Wallet.title: Wallet
Wallet.description: Represents a user's wallet for storing funds and tracking transactions.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a transaction in the user's wallet.

walletId.description: Reference to the Wallet. (Relationship: Wallet 1:N Transaction)

transactionType.description: Type of transaction (e.g., purchase, referral, withdrawal, profit).

transactionDate.description: Date and time of the transaction.

relatedEntityId.description: Reference to ID of the entity related to this Transaction, e.g. UserPackageId, WithdrawalRequestId. Can be null.

WithdrawalRequest.title: WithdrawalRequest
WithdrawalRequest.description: Represents a user's request to withdraw funds from their wallet.

id.description: Unique identifier for the withdrawal request.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the withdrawal request. (Relationship: User 1:N WithdrawalRequest)

requestDate.description: Date and time the withdrawal request was submitted.

status.description: Status of the withdrawal request (e.g., pending, approved, rejected).

adminId.description: Reference to the Admin who approved/rejected the request. (Relationship: User 1:N WithdrawalRequest)

transactionId.description: Reference to the Transaction associated with the withdrawal. (Relationship: Transaction 1:1 WithdrawalRequest)

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability for the SmartVest application. It incorporates denormalization to avoid hierarchical authorization dependencies, segregates data based on access needs, and uses consistent access modeling patterns. This structure supports secure `list` operations and maintains data integrity.

**Authorization Independence:**

*   **Users Collection:** The `isAdmin` field is directly embedded within each user document, removing the need to `get()` roles from a separate collection. This allows for atomic operations and simplifies security rules. Withdrawal requests are also linked to the user ID.

*   **Packages Collection:** Packages are managed by admins and are globally accessible to all users, eliminating the need for complex authorization logic. Each package can be independently read.

*   **UserPackages Collection:** Includes the `userId` to directly link the package to a specific user. This avoids needing to traverse the `users` collection to determine package ownership.

*   **Wallets and Transactions:** Wallets are owned by individual users, so the `walletId` and `userId` will facilitate secure access. Transactions are stored under wallets for easy querying.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   **Users Collection:** All user data is stored in a single collection. The `isAdmin` boolean differentiates admin from regular users.
*   **Packages Collection:** This collection stores all available packages, accessible to all users for reading but only writable by admins.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Private Data:** User-specific data (wallets, withdrawal requests, transactions) is stored in subcollections under the `/users/{userId}` path, enabling path-based ownership.
*   **Collaborative Data:** If the application involves collaborative features in future iterations, the membership map (`members: {uid1: 'role', uid2: 'role'}`) approach can be implemented within document for access control.

**QAPs Support:**

The design supports secure `list` operations (QAPs) through structural segregation and denormalization:

*   Listing packages is secure because the `/packages` collection contains only package data with uniform access requirements.
*   Listing a user's packages is secure because the `/users/{userId}/userPackages` subcollection is owned by that user, and the security rules can easily filter by the `userId`.

This structure facilitates simple and robust security rules, making the application more secure and easier to debug.
